biography: Rafael Daniel, born in the heart of São Paulo, Brazil, practically grew up on the fumes of race fuel. His father, a mechanic at Interlagos, often brought young Rafael to the track, instilling a deep love for speed and competition. Rafael started karting at 10, tearing through the local circuits with a raw talent that was immediately apparent. He quickly rose through the ranks, securing multiple regional karting championships. His transition to Copa Montana was a defining moment. Though he showed flashes of brilliance, consistency proved elusive, and he never quite secured a championship. A devastating crash at Tarumã in 2015, where he narrowly avoided serious injury, seemed to take the edge off his aggression. Now a veteran of the series, Rafael remains a popular figure, known for his flamboyant personality and occasional moments of brilliance, even if championship glory has remained out of reach.
drivingStyle: Rafael's driving style is best described as 'high-risk, high-reward.' He's known for aggressive overtaking maneuvers, often diving late into corners and relying on his car control to navigate through the chaos. While this approach can lead to spectacular passes, it also makes him prone to errors and collisions. Tire management is not his forte; he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, sacrificing long-term pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, Rafael can either crack or rise to the occasion, making him an unpredictable competitor.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial incident at Curitiba in 2012, where Rafael allegedly ran Ricardo off the track while battling for the lead.
A fierce on-track battle for position in the 2018 season finale led to multiple collisions and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.
A clash of personalities both on and off the track. Marco sees Rafael as reckless, while Rafael views Marco as overly cautious.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, even if they're falling apart.
Listens to a specific samba song before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to start a race if his car number is not perfectly aligned on the bodywork.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. You gotta push it to the limit, even if it means kissing the wall a little!"
careerHighlight: Winning the non-championship Interlagos Invitational race in 2010. The victory, celebrated wildly by his hometown fans, was a testament to his raw talent and the culmination of years of hard work.
careerLowPoint: The crash at Tarumã in 2015. Beyond the physical damage, the incident shook his confidence and led to a period of self-doubt that affected his performance for several seasons.
